root.name: Center Game: Normal Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. d4 exd4 3. Qxd4 Nc6

overview: White's early queen is hit by 3...Nc6 and retreats, usually 4.Qe3 (Paulsen Attack). White develops with Nc3, Bd2 or Bc4 and often castles long, hoping for a quick attack; Black develops calmly with ...Nf6, ...Be7 or ...g6 and equalises. The position is open and White gets a small lead in development but no lasting advantage.

white_ideas.idea: 4.Qe3, Nc3, Bd2, O-O-O, using the d-file and queen to attack.
Develop quickly and aim at g7 or the kingside.

black_ideas.idea: Gain tempi on the queen with ...Nc6 and ...Nf6.
Develop calmly and strike with ...d5 once ready.

typical_structures.structure: Open centre, half-open d-file for White, ...d5 break.

character.notes: Open and fairly equal; opposite-side castling occasionally races.

structure.notes: Open, since the centre pawns have been exchanged.

approach.notes: Played by strong players now and then.

level.notes: The early queen needs care but there is little theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Paulsen Attack
sublines_that_differ.how: The standard retreat, with long castling.

character.reason: Open and equal, neither forcing nor passive.

soundness.reason: Fully playable if Black plays accurately.

structure.reason: The d- and e-pawns are gone and pieces play on open lines.

approach.reason: Played by strong players now and then.

level.reason: Early-queen play needs care but little theory.

plans.reason: White's queen is out early and he aims to use his development.
